senses.definition: A part of the market made up of one industry, such as banking or healthcare.
senses.caution: Use it only for market segments. Promising to work one vertical at a time commits you to separate work for each industry, and people will ask which comes first.
senses.example: The core platform stays horizontal. We only build vertical-specific pieces where the regulator forces us to.

cues.text: An MD asks how you plan to expand next year. The answer is one sector at a time rather than one capability at a time, and you need the word for those market slices.
A sponsor wants to know why the healthcare build costs twice what the banking one did, and you need the term for the thing that makes them effectively different products.
You are writing a strategy note that separates what every client gets from what only insurers get, and you need a heading for the second category.
In a pipeline review someone asks why the same demo lands with logistics clients and falls flat with asset managers. You want the word for the split that explains it.

distractors: The underlying layer that everything above it runs on.
A basic building block a platform gives you and expects you to combine with others.
A funded team that holds a scarce skill in one place and sets how it is used.
One request splitting into many parallel pieces of work that run at the same time.
An isolated environment where code runs without touching anything real.
